document.title: Executive Order 13099, Prohibiting Transactions With Terrorists Who Threaten to Disrupt the Middle East Peace Process
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Terrorism and U.S. Policy
document.note: [Unclassified] Issued after the embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania, on the day of the retaliatory strikes in Afghanistan and Sudan. It amends EO 12947 to add Usama bin Ladin, the Al-Qaida organization and two other individuals to the list of those whose assets are blocked, and drops 'organizations' from the list heading. Federal Register Vol. 63, No. 164.

events.description: Executive Order 12947 declared a national emergency regarding terrorists threatening the Middle East peace process, creating the Annex of designated persons.
President Clinton signed EO 13099 adding bin Ladin, the Islamic Army (al-Qaida), Abu Hafs al-Masri and Rifa'i Ahmad Taha Musa to the Annex of EO 12947.
actors: Usama bin Muhammad bin Awad bin Ladin

events.description: EO 13099 became effective at 12:01 a.m. EDT.
Order published in the Federal Register, Vol. 63, No. 164.

President Clinton signed Executive Order 13099, adding Usama bin Ladin, the Islamic Army (Al-Qaida), Abu Hafs al-Masri and Rifa'i Ahmad Taha Musa to the Annex of Executive Order 12947 as terrorists who threaten to disrupt the Middle East peace process.
actors: Usama bin Muhammad bin Awad bin Ladin

events.description: Executive Order 13099 took effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time.
Executive Order 13099 was published in the Federal Register (Vol. 63, No. 164).
Executive Order 12947 was issued, declaring the national emergency and creating the Annex that EO 13099 amended.

key_claims: On 20 Aug 1998 the US designated Usama bin Ladin, the Islamic Army (al-Qaida), Abu Hafs al-Masri and Rifa'i Ahmad Taha Musa as terrorists threatening the Middle East peace process.
The US legally treated 'Islamic Army' as the primary name for al-Qaida, with multiple aliases including the World Islamic Front for Jihad Against Jews and Crusaders.
The designation extended the national emergency of EO 12947 (1995) to include these persons and the group, effective 21 Aug 1998.
